title: The Chronicle of ʿAlī ibn Turka

verdict.manText: He beat the tribunals that came and spent his last years waiting for the one that did not. The waiting was its own sentence.
verdict.systemText: The astrological-lettrist platform becomes the default imperial cosmology — Timurid, Aqquyunlu, Safavid, Uzbek, Ottoman, Mughal. Courts he never saw will run on his mathematics for centuries.

legacyNotes: He taught widely and hoarded jealously by turns — reach for the doctrine, reserve for its operative core — and the tension was never resolved, only lived.
He took Yazdī as a student. The roles did not hold, and both of them knew it early.
He let a doubtful miracle stand, and was counted among its witnesses.
He was of Akhlātī’s circle, whatever he later said about it.
He never took the bench, and faced every later accusation without an office behind him.
He told his family the truth about his work, and lived with what it cost him at their table.
He arrived at court as a jurist, and let them discover the rest at his own pace.
He served Bāysunghur, and the finest book-workshop in the world served him back.
He promised a prince a book rather than a marvel, and was quietly right to.
He delivered what he promised a patron — and every delivery raised the next demand.
He published an artisan’s discovery under his own name, and the workshops knew.
He forced his diagram to be plain enough for any copyist, against the atelier’s taste.
He refused to put his science into the army’s hands, more than once.
He attached himself to the surviving house, and was thereafter counted its man.
He kept a patron through the transition, and the protection was real when it was needed.
He wrote the summa as a working handbook, and the learned called it thin.
He refused even Yazdī a copy, and the summa stayed one object in one room.
Five students, taught everything: more than a secret, less than a movement.
He never drew the central figure, and his system was never afterward seen whole in one glance.
He met the first summons with a patron’s word behind him.
He won the first inquisition.
He wrote his own creed under pressure, and it was measured against everything he wrote after.
He never asked a patron to shield him, and met the tribunals on his own standing.
He declined the quiet arrangement, and the refusal was on file by evening.
The whole archive went to Yazdī, who outlived him by twenty-two years and lost nothing.
He corrected a popularizer’s errors and blessed the rest, and his system went where he could not follow.
He finished the system in exile — complete, in a rented room.
The Investigations exists. Whatever else is true, he wrote the book.
Yazdī copied the autograph in his own hand. That copy outlived them both.
While the tribunals sat he burned a court’s discreet commission unanswered.
He kept his science away from Scripture, and the jurists counted it to his credit.
He kept a prince’s table awake till dawn by art, and let a tired man sleep in peace.
He refused to write the bazaar its grimoire, and left that fortune for a later man.
His testament went out in small unsigned packets, exactly as durable as his friendships.

attested.hist: He studied in Cairo under Sayyid Ḥusayn Akhlāṭī, lettrist, alchemist and geomancer.
He served as Chief Judge of Isfahan, famous for defending the weak against the powerful.
attested.yours: you refused the bench he was defined by.

attested.hist: In 1420 he completed Investigations — the first systematic summa of Islamic lettrism — as Ulugh Beg broke ground on the Samarkand observatory.
His central diagram, the Ṭahawī Circle, survives in his own handwriting (Tehran, Majlis Library MS 10196, f. 63a).
attested.yours: you never drew the Circle; your system has no surviving image.

attested.hist: He faced three state inquisitions engineered by rival colleagues: he won the first two and lost the third, c. 1427.
attested.yours: the third tribunal never reached you.

attested.hist: Qāsim-i Anvār, his Cairo companion, was exiled in 1427 over the same lettrist associations.
attested.yours: in your life the friendship never came to its test.

attested.hist: He died in 1432, impoverished and in legal limbo, after five years of wandering exile; Yazdī — who copied his autograph — outlived him by twenty-two years, and the platform they built became imperial cosmology across six court cultures.
attested.yours: your Yazdī carries the copy too.

log.rubric: THE MERCHANT’S MAJLIS · A WANDERER’S IMPOSSIBLE CLAIM
log.source: Design conversation, Node 11 — credulity vs. demonstration; later manuals attest the type
log.situation: A traveling dervish holds the salon rapt: he claims he can be in Cairo and Damascus in the same night, and has witnesses. The merchant, your host, turns to you — the studious one — and asks, smiling, whether it can be true.

plate.caption: The Seven Sleepers of Ephesus, folio from a Falnāma — Book of Omens (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Examine the claim like an apparatus
options.detail: It takes a trickster’s eye to catch one. Ask what, exactly, the witnesses saw.

options.label: Reframe it philosophically
options.detail: Neither endorse nor expose: ask what “being in a place” means. Scholars love it.

options.label: Let the wonder stand
options.detail: Say nothing against it. The room wants marvels; the dervish needs dinner.

log.outcomeText: The story swells with your silence inside it. Later you hear your name cited among those who “did not deny it.”

chronicle.orig: He let a doubtful wonder pass unchallenged, and was counted among its witnesses.
chronicle.current: He let a doubtful wonder pass unchallenged, and was counted among its witnesses.

log.rubric: THE MERCHANT’S MAJLIS · THE HOST WANTS A WONDER
log.source: Bazm culture per The Occult Court; the request type attested in later manuals
log.situation: The wine has gone round twice and the merchant claps for entertainment — and looks at you. “Our scholar! Show us something the preachers wouldn’t like.” The room laughs. Whatever happens in the next ten minutes will be retold.

plate.caption: Winged angels, al-Qazwīnī’s Wonders of Creation (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Perform a real wonder, properly
options.detail: Rīmiyā, done with craft: astonish them, and control exactly what they saw.

options.label: Give them Qāsim’s verses instead
options.detail: Borrow your friend’s thunder — a performance no preacher can indict.

options.label: Attempt sleight-of-hand untrained
options.detail: You have watched it done. How hard can a vanishing coin be?

options.label: Decline, with a jurist’s smile
options.detail: Disappoint the room; reassure the careful. Nothing retold, nothing risked.

log.outcomeText: The merchant pouts and finds a lute-player. You are, everyone agrees, no fun — and quite safe.

chronicle.orig: Pressed for marvels at the feast, he declined with a jurist’s exact courtesy.
chronicle.current: Pressed for marvels at the feast, he declined with a jurist’s exact courtesy.

log.rubric: THE TIMEKEEPER’S POST · INSTRUMENTS AND HOURS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Formation; the muwaqqit’s office was Cairo’s licensed astronomy
log.situation: The mosque’s muwaqqit — the timekeeper — computes the prayer hours with astrolabe and tables, the one occult-adjacent mathematics no jurist can object to. He needs an assistant with steady hands and will teach what the position teaches.

options.label: Assist him through a season
options.detail: Learn the astrolabe and the tables — licensed mathematics, unimpeachable.

options.label: Watch a single night’s working
options.detail: One evening’s glimpse of the craft — cheap, shallow, enough to know what’s there.

log.outcomeText: One night at the dials. You leave knowing exactly how much you do not know.

chronicle.orig: He watched the timekeeper work one night, and marked the science for later.
chronicle.current: He watched the timekeeper work one night, and marked the science for later.

log.rubric: THE TIMEKEEPER’S POST · ANOTHER PERSIAN AT THE DIALS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Formation: the Yazdī friendship (VN c03); meeting-place is PLAUSIBLE-GAP
log.situation: Another Persian keeps turning up at the tables: Sharaf al-Dīn ʿAlī of Yazd, who checks the muwaqqit’s arithmetic for pleasure and talks about history the way you talk about letters. He has noticed you noticing him.

options.label: Meet him as an equal — trade everything
options.detail: Two minds, no hierarchy. Your letters for his mathematics, openly.

options.label: Take the senior part — teach, don’t trade
options.detail: Guide the younger man. Generous — and it sets the friendship’s shape early.

log.outcomeText: He learns fast — faster than a student should. You suspect the roles will not hold, and you are right.

chronicle.orig: He took Yazdī as a student, though anyone watching could see what the friendship would become.
chronicle.current: He took Yazdī as a student, though anyone watching could see what the friendship would become.

log.rubric: THE BOOKSELLERS’ BAZAAR · AN UNATTRIBUTED TREATISE
log.source: Design conversation, “The New Manuscript” pattern; bazaar trade attested
log.situation: A dealer who knows your haunts unrolls something unsigned: tables pairing letters to numbers to stations of the moon, in a hand nobody recognizes. He wants a week’s wages for it. Three other men in Cairo would want it more.

plate.caption: Letter-word wafq table, Quranic name operations grid — Princeton University Library

options.label: Test its number-structure before buying
options.detail: Check the grids against what Akhlāṭī taught you. Fraud has a signature.

options.label: Bring Akhlāṭī to see it quietly
options.detail: The master’s eye is surer than yours — and the dealer will notice whose.

options.label: Let it go
options.detail: A week’s wages is a week’s wages. Some doors are better unopened.

log.outcomeText: It sells within the day — to whom, the dealer will not say. You will wonder about this for years.

chronicle.orig: He let the unsigned treatise pass to an unknown buyer, and remembered it long after.
chronicle.current: He let the unsigned treatise pass to an unknown buyer, and remembered it long after.

log.rubric: AT THE KHĀNQĀH · A POET IN FULL FLIGHT
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Formation: Qāsim-i Anvār a close Cairo companion (VN c04)
log.situation: Qāsim-i Anvār recites and the whole khānqāh forgets to breathe. Afterward he finds you, laughing, quoting your own question back at you improved. Men like this either become your brother or your epitaph. Sometimes both.

options.label: Let the friendship go deep
options.detail: Brotherhood with the most magnetic — and least careful — man in Cairo.

options.label: Keep a warm distance
options.detail: Enjoy the verses; skip the entanglement. Poets attract weather.

log.outcomeText: He notices, of course. Poets always notice. The verses stay brilliant; the door stays ajar.

chronicle.orig: He admired Qāsim-i Anvār from one careful step away.
chronicle.current: He admired Qāsim-i Anvār from one careful step away.

log.rubric: A COURTYARD OFF THE COPPERSMITHS’ STREET · AFTER DARK
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Formation (Cairo): studied under Akhlāṭī
log.situation: Sayyid Ḥusayn Akhlāṭī receives students the madrasa would never admit to envying. On his table: letter-tables, a geomancer’s brass instrument, a crucible still warm. He asks one question — what do you want to learn first?

plate.caption: Geomantic instrument, Egypt or Syria, 1241/42 CE — British Museum (via Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: The science of letters
options.detail: Līmiyā: talismans, letter-grids, the mathematics hiding inside the alphabet.

options.label: The work of the furnace
options.detail: Kīmiyā: substances, operations, the elite and expensive art.

options.label: The figures in the sand
options.detail: Geomancy — Akhlāṭī’s own third art, quick to learn, easy to sneer at, oddly reliable.

log.outcomeText: He hands you the bellows first, and theory second. The door is open.

chronicle.orig: He came to Akhlāṭī’s courtyard and learned the furnace before the theory of it.
chronicle.current: He came to Akhlāṭī’s courtyard and learned the furnace before the theory of it.

log.rubric: THE ROAD HOME · CAIRO ENDS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Formation: Akhlāṭī dies 1397; the return to Iran follows
log.situation: Word runs through the quarter like cold water: Sayyid Ḥusayn Akhlāṭī is dead. The circle stands in his courtyard not knowing where to put its hands. Cairo is finished for you — the question is only what you carry to Isfahan, and how.

plate.caption: Teardrop cosmological diagram — Shams al-Maʿārif, p. 256 (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Leave as his acknowledged student
options.detail: Claim the inheritance aloud. The name will reach Isfahan before you do.

options.label: Carry the Brethren’s letters east
options.detail: Leave as the network’s courier: introductions from Cairo to all Iran.

options.label: Return as a jurist, nothing more
options.detail: Fold the Cairo years away. Arrive in Isfahan clean, credentialed, unremarked.

options.label: Travel in company with Yazdī
options.detail: Share the road with your brother in God. The system’s first two carriers, together.

log.outcomeText: You travel as a judge’s son returning with a judge’s learning. What else you carry, you carry inside.

chronicle.orig: He returned to Isfahan as a jurist returns: quietly, with his true baggage invisible.
chronicle.current: He returned to Isfahan as a jurist returns: quietly, with his true baggage invisible.

log.rubric: YOUR OWN STUDY · THE LETTERS AND THE NUMBERS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — mathematization of the cosmos; lettrism as universal science
log.situation: A long night with the tables. The correspondence between letter-values and the ratios in a musical interval is either the deepest thing you have ever noticed or an artifact of your own arithmetic. There is one way to find out.

options.label: Work it through to the end
options.detail: Seasons of arithmetic to prove or kill the connection.

options.label: Note it and move on
options.detail: The docket will not wait. Write it down for a better decade.

log.outcomeText: Into the notebook it goes, with a marginal note you will find again in 1420.

chronicle.orig: He noted the harmonic correspondence and set it aside for a freer year.
chronicle.current: He noted the harmonic correspondence and set it aside for a freer year.

log.rubric: THE FRIDAY MOSQUE · A SERMON AGAINST THE LETTER-MEN
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — the orthodoxy/lettrism tension; this sermon is constructed
log.situation: The Friday preacher spends a quarter of an hour on men who claim the letters of the Qurʾan hide a mathematics. He does not name you. He does not need to; two rows of heads have already half-turned.

options.label: Answer him after the prayer, in front of everyone
options.detail: Meet it head-on as a jurist. High risk, high clarity.

options.label: Seek him privately afterward
options.detail: Persuade one man instead of a hall. Quiet, slow, sometimes it works.

options.label: Sit through it
options.detail: Say nothing. Be seen saying nothing. Perfectly safe, and everyone notices.

log.outcomeText: He is polite, immovable, and now knows your face and your interest.

chronicle.orig: His private approach to the preacher changed nothing except that the preacher now knew him.
chronicle.current: His private approach to the preacher changed nothing except that the preacher now knew him.

log.rubric: ISFAHAN · A MERCHANT WANTS HIS SON’S NATIVITY READ
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — astrological practice; this client is constructed
log.situation: A wealthy merchant wants to know whether his son should be sent into trade or into the law. He is offering good money for a nativity. He is also, without meaning to, offering you your first paying client as a practitioner.

plate.caption: Astrological figure from a Book of Nativities, after Abū Maʿshar al-Balkhī (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Cast the nativity properly
options.detail: Real computation, honest reading, fair fee.

options.label: Read the boy’s name, not his stars
options.detail: Lettrism instead of astrology — your own method, on a stranger, for money.

options.label: Advise him as a judge, and take nothing
options.detail: Give the boy sound counsel with no stars in it. No fee, no practice, no exposure.

log.outcomeText: You tell him to ask the boy. The merchant leaves obscurely disappointed and entirely safe to know.

chronicle.orig: Asked for a nativity, he gave a judge’s advice and refused the fee.
chronicle.current: Asked for a nativity, he gave a judge’s advice and refused the fee.

log.rubric: THE WARRĀQ’S SHOP · A MAN WHO COPIES ANYTHING
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — manuscript culture; this copyist is constructed
log.situation: The warrāq works fast, charges fairly, and has never once asked what a text is for. Everything you have written so far exists in exactly one copy, in your own hand, in a house that could burn.

options.label: Commission copies of your notes
options.detail: Transmission begins with a second copy existing at all.

options.label: Copy everything in your own hand
options.detail: Slower, safer, and no stranger has read a line of it.

log.outcomeText: Seasons of copying. The work is exact, secure, and read by precisely one person.

chronicle.orig: He copied his own work in his own hand, and let no stranger read a line of it.
chronicle.current: He copied his own work in his own hand, and let no stranger read a line of it.

log.rubric: THE FAMILY HOUSE · WHAT THE HOUSE EXPECTS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — the Turka family judicial line; the domestic scene is constructed
log.situation: Your kin want to know what Cairo was for. There is a family library of law and hadith, a family reputation, and a family assumption that the strange years abroad are now concluded.

options.label: Tell them what they want to hear
options.detail: Cairo was training. Nothing more. The house relaxes.

options.label: Tell them the truth and ask for the library
options.detail: Make the family an asset instead of an audience. Risky; they vote.

log.outcomeText: The word "lettrist" lands badly at a family dinner. Doors do not slam; they simply stop opening.

chronicle.orig: He told his family the truth about the Cairo years, and the house grew cooler by a degree.
chronicle.current: He told his family the truth about the Cairo years, and the house grew cooler by a degree.

log.rubric: THE TRIBUNAL · THE OFFICE OFFERED
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Vitals: Chief Judge (qāḍī) of Isfahan
log.situation: The bench your father sat on is open, and the city expects a Turka on it. The office pays, protects, and confers the one credential no accusation slides off easily: you would be a judge, not merely a man with opinions.

options.label: Take the judgeship
options.detail: Salary, standing, and a permanent claim on your hours.

options.label: Refuse the bench
options.detail: Keep every hour for the work. Lose the shield the office would have been.

options.label: Serve, but seek a deputy first
options.detail: Take the office and immediately find someone to carry half of it.

log.outcomeText: The city is puzzled; your kin are worse than puzzled. Your hours, though, are your own.

chronicle.orig: He declined the judgeship of Isfahan, and kept his hours for the work.
chronicle.current: He declined the judgeship of Isfahan, and kept his hours for the work.

log.rubric: YOUR OWN STUDY · THE MYSTERIOUS LETTERS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Qurʾanic letter-groups (muqaṭṭaʿāt) in the lettrist tradition; Yazdī’s practice
log.situation: The disconnected letters that open certain sūras — alif lām mīm, ṭā hā — have defeated commentary for eight centuries. Every exegete says they are a divine secret. You are increasingly sure they are a divine *notation*.

plate.caption: Budūh magic square, al-Qazwīnī — Persia, c. 1280 (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Treat them as notation and build the system on them
options.detail: The boldest move available: make the unexplained letters your foundation stone.

options.label: Handle them reverently and stay inside commentary
options.detail: Say what the tradition says. Lose the foundation stone; keep the peace.

log.outcomeText: You write a careful, orthodox, unremarkable page on the letter-groups, and know exactly what you left out of it.

chronicle.orig: He wrote on the mysterious letters within the bounds of commentary, and left his real thought unwritten.
chronicle.current: He wrote on the mysterious letters within the bounds of commentary, and left his real thought unwritten.

log.rubric: THE SUMMONS · A PRINCE SENDS FOR YOU
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — attachment to Iskandar Sultan’s court c. 1409
log.situation: A courier in Timurid livery, a sealed letter, and an invitation that is not really one: Iskandar Sultan, prince and governor of Fars, has heard there is a judge in Isfahan who reads more than law. The Isfahan years end here.

options.label: Go, and bring the whole apparatus
options.detail: Books, tables, instruments, ambitions. Arrive as what you actually are.

options.label: Go as a jurist, and let them discover the rest
options.detail: Arrive credentialed and unremarkable. Reveal the work when the room is right.

options.label: Go, and bring your people
options.detail: A copyist, a correspondent, a friend. Arrive as a circle, not a man.

log.outcomeText: You arrive as a judge of good family. What else you are can wait for a better evening.

chronicle.orig: He came to the prince’s court as a jurist, and kept his other science in the baggage.
chronicle.current: He came to the prince’s court as a jurist, and kept his other science in the baggage.

log.rubric: THE KITĀBKHĀNA · THE CALLIGRAPHER HAS FOUND A PATTERN
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Bāysunghur’s atelier and calligraphic culture; this calligrapher is constructed
log.situation: The court calligrapher has been laying out a square Kufic panel and has noticed that the letters, forced into a grid, generate the same proportions in three different verses. She wants to know whether she has found something or merely made something. It is, exactly, your question.

plate.caption: Square Kufic Bismillah page by Ahmed Karahisari, 16th c. (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Work it out with her
options.detail: Take an artisan seriously as a colleague. Gains a capability, not a compliment.

options.label: Take the observation and thank her
options.detail: It is a real finding. It can be yours. She is an artisan; nobody will ask.

options.label: Tell her it is an artifact of the grid
options.detail: Probably true. Definitely discouraging. Costs you nothing and closes a door.

log.outcomeText: The finding is genuinely useful. The workshop is a small world, and workshops talk to each other.

chronicle.orig: He published the calligrapher’s observation as his own, and the workshop noticed.
chronicle.current: He published the calligrapher’s observation as his own, and the workshop noticed.

log.rubric: THE AUDIENCE HALL · WHOSE MAN WILL YOU BE
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Iskandar Sultan (c.1409–1415), then Bāysunghur (from c.1416)
log.situation: Two houses want you, and a third possibility exists. Iskandar Sultan’s court at Shiraz fuses star science, poetry and painting — brilliant and politically exposed. Bāysunghur, Shāh Rukh’s son, offers the finest book-workshop in the world and a father who is currently winning. Samarkand offers mathematics and Ulugh Beg.

options.label: Take service with Iskandar Sultan
options.detail: The experimental court: everything permitted, nothing guaranteed.

options.label: Take service with Bāysunghur
options.detail: The manuscript machine, and the safer branch of the dynasty.

options.label: Go to Samarkand with Yazdī
options.detail: Mathematics, instruments, and the observatory rising. Requires your brother in God.

log.outcomeText: Bāysunghur, who is himself a calligrapher of the first rank, asks what your diagrams would look like properly made. Nobody has ever asked you that.

chronicle.orig: He took service with Bāysunghur, a prince who cared how a page was made.
chronicle.current: He took service with Bāysunghur, a prince who cared how a page was made.

log.rubric: THE CAMPAIGN · AN ARMY THAT IS NOT THERE
log.source: RESEARCH — later manuals catalogue suffumigation operations producing giant smoke figures, one framed as a trick played on Alexander; the application here is constructed
log.situation: A commander with a thin garrison and a wide frontier has heard — from a feast, from a rumor, from somewhere — that the old manuals describe smokes that read at distance as giant figures, even armies. The books do describe them. They also describe men who tried such compounds and produced only a smell. He wants to know if it can be done.

plate.caption: Demons, Kitāb al-Bulhān — Baghdad, late 14th–15th c. (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Attempt the great suffumigation
options.detail: Sīmiyā at campaign scale: compounds, wind, and an enemy’s imagination.

options.label: Tell him what the books do not say
options.detail: The epistemology option: separate the tested from the wished-for, in writing.

options.label: Decline the whole question
options.detail: War-work again. You have refused it before; refuse it again.

log.outcomeText: You decline. The commander finds a cheaper practitioner whose smoke does nothing, which costs him only money.

chronicle.orig: He refused the army’s smoke, and a cheaper man sold them fog.
chronicle.current: He refused the army’s smoke, and a cheaper man sold them fog.

log.rubric: THE FEAST · SOMETHING TO ASTONISH THE TABLE
log.source: RESEARCH — bazm/razm as the poles of Timurid court culture; wonder-working at feasts attested in the later manuals
log.situation: Deep into the bazm, the prince wants a wonder and everyone is drunk enough to want it badly. This is not a lesser occasion than the audience hall. Half the political business of this court is done exactly here, in jokes.

plate.caption: Winged angels, al-Qazwīnī’s Wonders of Creation (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: The vanishing ink
options.detail: Write, let them read, let it disappear. Delightful — and quietly useful to certain people.

options.label: Give them a number-riddle instead
options.detail: Teach a little mathematics disguised as a game. Safer, and it sticks.

options.label: Perform something frankly ridiculous
options.detail: The court likes to laugh. Laughter is medicine, says the tradition, and it disarms watchers.

log.outcomeText: Three courtiers are still arguing about it at breakfast. One of them will ask you to explain it properly, which is how a student is acquired.

chronicle.orig: At the feast he set a number-riddle, and won a student by it in the morning.
chronicle.current: At the feast he set a number-riddle, and won a student by it in the morning.

log.rubric: THE FEAST · LATE, AND THE VIZIER IS ASLEEP
log.source: RESEARCH — later manuals describe sleeper-interrogation and wake-rite operations among feast entertainments; this scene is constructed around those categories
log.situation: Deep in the night-half of the bazm, a junior vizier has fallen asleep sitting upright, and the prince — delighted, a little drunk — remembers a story: that the old manuals teach how to make a sleeping man answer questions truthfully. Everyone looks at you. The vizier snores. The room is already composing the anecdote.

plate.caption: The Singer Ibrāhīm and the Jinn — Iran, early modern copy (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Perform it as theater
options.detail: Rīmiyā: stage-whisper, planted questions, harmless answers. The room gets its story; the vizier keeps his secrets.

options.label: Refuse — and say why
options.detail: A sleeping man cannot consent to be a demonstration. Kill the joke; keep the principle.

options.label: Offer the opposite trick instead
options.detail: The wake-rite: keep the whole table alert till dawn. Redirect the room’s appetite.

log.outcomeText: A preparation from the manuals — mostly strong ingredients and stronger theater — and the feast runs to sunrise with nobody asleep to mock. The kitchen bills you personally.

chronicle.orig: He kept the prince’s table awake until dawn by art, and let the sleeping man sleep.
chronicle.current: He kept the prince’s table awake until dawn by art, and let the sleeping man sleep.

log.rubric: THE FEAST · WHO EVERYONE ACTUALLY IS
log.source: RESEARCH — confessional and factional ambiguity in occultist circles; legal, Sufi and confessional identities did not align neatly
log.situation: Late, and the table has thinned to the people who stay late. A jurist here is quietly devoted to the Prophet’s family; a Sufi turns out to be rigorous in law; the prince’s secretary is reading something he should not have. None of these identities line up the way the labels promise. Someone will ask where you stand.

options.label: Answer differently to each of them
options.detail: The translation mechanic in miniature: same doctrine, four registers.

options.label: Give all of them the same answer
options.detail: One doctrine, undiluted, whoever is listening. Consistent, and it makes enemies honestly.

options.label: Turn the question into a joke and go to bed
options.detail: Nothing said, nothing owed, nothing gained.

log.outcomeText: The joke is good enough that nobody presses. You leave with your positions intact and unknown.

chronicle.orig: Asked where he stood at the late table, he made a joke and went to bed.
chronicle.current: Asked where he stood at the late table, he made a joke and went to bed.

log.rubric: THE KITĀBKHĀNA · THE MONUMENTAL QURʾAN
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Bāysunghur as likely commissioner of the monumental Bāysunghur Qurʾan; VN c12
log.situation: The kitābkhāna is preparing the largest Qurʾan ever attempted — pages taller than a man, a monument in ink. Bāysunghur asks, in the manner of a prince who already suspects the answer, whether the science of letters has anything to say about how the Word of God should be laid upon a page that size.

plate.caption: Square Kufic Bismillah page by Ahmed Karahisari, 16th c. (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Offer a lettrist framework for the layout
options.detail: Your proportions, in the most permanent object this dynasty will make. Glory, in evidence form.

options.label: Advise the calligraphers privately
options.detail: Influence without authorship. Nothing to point at; nothing to indict.

options.label: Keep your science away from Scripture
options.detail: The one place a lettrist should perhaps not practice. Safe, and a renunciation.

log.outcomeText: You decline with a formula about the Word needing no improvement. The jurists who hear of it approve. The calligraphers, oddly, seem disappointed.

chronicle.orig: Asked to bring his science to the great Qurʾan, he declined, and the jurists marked it in his favor.
chronicle.current: Asked to bring his science to the great Qurʾan, he declined, and the jurists marked it in his favor.

log.rubric: THE KITĀBKHĀNA · YOUR DIAGRAM, PROPERLY MADE
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Bāysunghur as accomplished calligrapher and patron of the book arts
log.situation: The kitābkhāna offers to make one of your cosmological diagrams the way it makes things for princes: gold, lapis, a full folio. A diagram that beautiful is an argument that travels — and a diagram that beautiful is also evidence.

plate.caption: Safavid illuminated manuscript page, Shahnameh tradition (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Let them make it magnificent
options.detail: Gold and lapis. The system becomes an object princes want to own.

options.label: Insist on a plain, teachable version
options.detail: Simple, explained, reproducible by any copyist. Designed for uptake, not for princes.

options.label: Keep the diagram out of the workshop
options.detail: No copies, no folio, no evidence. The cleanest way to stay small.

log.outcomeText: The illuminators are baffled and slightly offended. The result can be copied by anyone with a reed pen, which is the entire point.

chronicle.orig: He insisted his diagram be made plain enough for any copyist, against the atelier’s better taste.
chronicle.current: He insisted his diagram be made plain enough for any copyist, against the atelier’s better taste.

log.rubric: THE AUDIENCE HALL · THE PATRON WANTS SOMETHING USEFUL
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — works commissioned as royal "boons"; patronage was transactional and explicit
log.situation: The commission is put plainly, which is how commissions are put: something demonstrable, by a named season, in exchange for money and standing. The prince does not want a philosophy. He wants a result he can show people.

options.label: Promise a public demonstration
options.detail: The big claim. Big reward if you land it — and a promise a court can measure.

options.label: Promise a written exposition instead
options.detail: Smaller claim, likelier delivery. Patrons remember who does not miss.

options.label: Negotiate the terms down
options.detail: Longer deadline, smaller reward. The professional’s answer.

options.label: Decline the commission
options.detail: Take no money and make no promise. Costs standing; costs nothing else.

log.outcomeText: A book, then, by the fourth season. He seems mildly disappointed and entirely satisfied.

chronicle.orig: He undertook to write the prince an exposition rather than promise him a spectacle.
chronicle.current: He undertook to write the prince an exposition rather than promise him a spectacle.

log.rubric: TOWARD 1420 · THE COURT YEARS END
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Iskandar Sultan defeated, blinded and executed 1415; patronage shifts to Bāysunghur c.1416
log.situation: Courts end. Iskandar Sultan overreached his uncle Shāh Rukh and paid for it in the way Timurid princes do; the workshops disperse, the patronage reshuffles, and men who were somebody last spring are looking for a house. What you take out of these years is the material the summa will be built from.

plate.caption: "Caesar Makes a Talisman", folio from a Shahnama, Iran c. 1330–40 — MET (CC0)

options.label: Leave with the work, and nothing else
options.detail: Books, tables, diagrams. Let the politics go on without you.

options.label: Attach yourself to the surviving house
options.detail: Bāysunghur’s establishment endures. Continuity of protection, at the price of visible loyalty.

options.label: Leave with your people
options.detail: Calligrapher, astronomer, student, friend — whoever will come. The circle over the career.

log.outcomeText: You are absorbed into the winning household. Protection now; a documented association forever.

chronicle.orig: He attached himself to the surviving princely house, and was thereafter counted its man.
chronicle.current: He attached himself to the surviving princely house, and was thereafter counted its man.

log.rubric: THE OBSERVATORY RISING · ULUGH BEG BREAKS GROUND
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — 1420: Ulugh Beg begins the Samarkand observatory; star science and letter science boom together
log.situation: In Samarkand they are laying the foundations of the largest astronomical instrument on earth. The tables it produces will still be in use in London four centuries from now. Nobody there is thinking about lettrism — but the man building it wants exact knowledge of the heavens, and so, in your own way, do you.

options.label: Put your mathematics at their disposal
options.detail: Work on the tables. Anonymous, rigorous, and it ties your name to real science.

options.label: Argue that star science and letter science are one enterprise
options.detail: Make the case to the astronomers themselves. If it lands, it is the whole thesis vindicated.

options.label: Stay at your desk
options.detail: Samarkand is a distraction. The summa will not write itself.

log.outcomeText: You keep working. The greatest observatory in the world goes up without you, and your book gets better.

chronicle.orig: He stayed at his desk while the observatory rose without him.
chronicle.current: He stayed at his desk while the observatory rose without him.

log.rubric: THE DESK · BEGINNING THE SUMMA
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — 1420: completes Investigations (Kitāb al-Mafāḥiṣ), the first systematic summa of Islamic lettrism
log.situation: Twenty years of notes, and the shape of the thing is finally visible: not a commentary, not a manual, but a systematic philosophy in which letter, number, and cosmos are one science. It has never been done. The only question is what kind of book it will be.

options.label: Build it as a complete philosophical system
options.detail: The whole architecture, argued from first principles. Slow, enormous, and unprecedented.

options.label: Build it as a usable handbook
options.detail: Method first, philosophy implicit. Less glory, far more uptake.

options.label: Not yet — spend the year deepening instead
options.detail: Refuse to publish prematurely. The system gets better; the years do not come back.

log.outcomeText: A working book: definitions, procedures, worked examples. Scholars will call it thin. Practitioners will actually use it.

chronicle.orig: He wrote the summa as a working handbook, and the learned called it thin.
chronicle.current: He wrote the summa as a working handbook, and the learned called it thin.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · YAZDĪ ASKS FOR THE AUTOGRAPH
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Yazdī likely copies Ibn Turka’s own autograph, ff. 52a–56a of Tehran Majlis MS 10196, c. 1420–25
log.situation: Yazdī wants to copy the autograph in his own hand — not have it copied, copy it himself, which between the two of you means something. He is becoming the historian who writes dynasties into the heavens. What he carries, the century carries.

options.label: Give him the autograph
options.detail: The single highest-leverage act available to you. A copy in his hand outlives you both.

options.label: Work through it with him, line by line
options.detail: Not just a copy — a transfer. Slow, and it makes him a co-author of the transmission.

options.label: Keep the autograph in your own keeping
options.detail: One copy, one hand, total control. And a house that could burn.

log.outcomeText: He does not argue. He is disappointed in a way that will not be mentioned again, and the summa remains a single object in a single room.

chronicle.orig: He refused even Yazdī a copy of the autograph, and the summa stayed one object in one room.
chronicle.current: He refused even Yazdī a copy of the autograph, and the summa stayed one object in one room.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · WHO GETS THE KNOWLEDGE
log.source: RESEARCH — de-esotericization and democratization as defining features of this occult-scientific culture; hoard-prestige vs. teach-for-reach as a real axis
log.situation: They keep coming: a persistent student who has copied everything you ever circulated, two correspondents from Shiraz, a young jurist who asks better questions than your colleagues. You can build a school, or you can build a secret. The tradition says the second. The century, increasingly, is doing the first.

options.label: Teach anyone who comes
options.detail: Maximum transmission. You will lose control of the doctrine and gain a movement.

options.label: Take a handful of qualified students only
options.detail: Depth over reach. A real school, small enough to control.

options.label: Teach no one
options.detail: The book is the teaching. Anyone worthy will find it. Very traditional; very risky.

log.outcomeText: Five students, properly trained, who understand the operative layer and can be trusted with it. Fewer than a movement; more than a secret.

chronicle.orig: He took five students and taught them everything, which was more than a secret and less than a movement.
chronicle.current: He took five students and taught them everything, which was more than a secret and less than a movement.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · THE POPULAR COMMISSION
log.source: VN c24; the Boon-for-the-Khan pattern — named-operation manuals for broad audiences — is attested a generation later
log.situation: A bookseller’s consortium makes a proposal with real money in it: not the summa — nobody can sell the summa — but a manual. Named operations, numbered steps, results promised: the vanishing inks, the wake-rites, the figures in sand. The kind of book that sells in every bazaar and follows its author into every courtroom.

options.label: Write the practical manual
options.detail: Reach and income. A hundred bazaars; also a hundred witnesses.

options.label: Counter-offer the elite commission
options.detail: Kīmiyā standing lets you propose the expensive book instead: fewer buyers, better ones.

options.label: Decline the trade entirely
options.detail: The summa is the legacy. Keep the operations out of the bazaar.

log.outcomeText: You decline. A generation later, someone else will write exactly this book and grow famous on it — a fact you will be spared knowing.

chronicle.orig: He refused to write the bazaar its manual, and left that fortune for a later man.
chronicle.current: He refused to write the bazaar its manual, and left that fortune for a later man.

log.rubric: THE DRAWING BOARD · THE ṬAHAWĪ CIRCLE
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — the Ṭahawī Circle, first "modern" lettrist reworking of the Pythagorean Tetractys; survives in Ibn Turka’s own autograph (Tehran, Majlis MS 10196, f. 63a)
log.situation: The system needs one image that holds it all: the Pythagorean Tetractys, rebuilt in letters. Get this right and a reader grasps in one glance what the prose takes four hundred pages to argue. Get it wrong and the whole edifice looks like decoration.

plate.caption: Persian wafq — a 6×6 magic square with instructions, 16th c. (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Draw the Circle, and draw it simply
options.detail: The signature diagram, designed to be understood and copied.

options.label: Make it magnificent instead of simple
options.detail: A diagram princes will hang. Impressive; harder to teach from.

options.label: Argue it in prose; draw nothing
options.detail: No diagram to be seized, quoted, or misread. Also no image anyone remembers.

log.outcomeText: The argument stands without a picture. Nobody will ever be able to hold your system in their head all at once, including your students.

chronicle.orig: He left the central figure undrawn, and his system was never afterward seen whole in one glance.
chronicle.current: He left the central figure undrawn, and his system was never afterward seen whole in one glance.

log.rubric: THE FIRST SUMMONS · A TRIBUNAL SENDS FOR YOU
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — three state inquisitions, engineered by jealous rival colleagues, from the 1420s
log.situation: It arrives with a seal and a date: you are required to answer questions concerning your doctrine. It is not, yet, a trial. It has been engineered by colleagues — men who know exactly what to quote, because you wrote it down and let it circulate. The rest of your life begins with this letter.

options.label: Go, and prepare a full defense
options.detail: Answer the summons on its own terms, with everything you have.

options.label: Go, but send to your patron first
options.detail: Spend political protection before spending arguments.

options.label: Go quietly, and concede whatever is cheap
options.detail: Give them small things early. Survive the first one; think about the rest later.

log.outcomeText: Word goes to the household that pays you. Protection is a real thing; it is also a debt, and debts are collected.

chronicle.orig: Summoned, he sent first to his patron and then to his books.
chronicle.current: Summoned, he sent first to his patron and then to his books.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · WHAT TO DO WITH THE MANUSCRIPTS
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — Investigations remains understudied for centuries, effectively "on the Index"; this dispersal scene is constructed
log.situation: If the third tribunal goes badly, everything in this room becomes evidence. Your student is willing to carry copies out tonight; your instinct is to keep the autograph where you can defend it. Paper survives men, but only if it is somewhere else.

options.label: Disperse copies to four cities
options.detail: No single seizure can end the work. Control lost, survival bought.

options.label: Send everything to Yazdī
options.detail: One trusted hand, at the observatory, protected by an institution.

options.label: Keep everything with you
options.detail: Defend it in person, or lose it in person.

log.outcomeText: He takes it all to Samarkand without comment. He will outlive you by twenty-two years and he does not lose things.

chronicle.orig: He sent the whole archive to Yazdī, who outlived him by twenty-two years and lost nothing.
chronicle.current: He sent the whole archive to Yazdī, who outlived him by twenty-two years and lost nothing.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · SOMEONE HAS SIMPLIFIED YOU
log.source: RESEARCH — the Kāshifī/ʿAlī Ṣafī "Everyman’s Library" simplifications of the same material for wider circulation
log.situation: A book is circulating that is unmistakably your system, in easy Persian, with the difficulties removed and someone else’s name on it. It is selling. It is also, in three places, wrong — and in two places, better than what you wrote.

options.label: Denounce it
options.detail: Defend the doctrine’s integrity. Public, principled, and it advertises the book.

options.label: Correct the errors and endorse the rest
options.detail: Accept that reach costs precision. Fix what matters; let the rest go.

options.label: Ignore it
options.detail: You have a tribunal to prepare for. Let the century sort it out.

log.outcomeText: Corrections accepted, approval printed. Purists in your own circle are appalled, which you can live with.

chronicle.orig: He endorsed a simplified version of his own work, to his students’ dismay.
chronicle.current: He endorsed a simplified version of his own work, to his students’ dismay.

log.rubric: THE PATRON’S DOOR · ASKING FOR PROTECTION
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — patronage as political protection; this specific appeal is constructed
log.situation: The household that has paid you for a decade can make a tribunal go away, and knows it. The steward makes you wait, which is the message. Protection is available. It is not free, and it is not unlimited.

options.label: Ask outright
options.detail: Spend the relationship on your safety. It works; it also ends something.

options.label: Offer something first
options.detail: Arrive with a gift, not a request. A horoscope, a dedication, a useful method.

options.label: Do not ask
options.detail: Face the tribunals on your own standing. Clean, and much harder.

log.outcomeText: You go home without asking. Whatever happens at the tribunal will be yours, which is either dignity or vanity and you are not sure which.

chronicle.orig: He never asked his patron to shield him, and met the tribunals on his own standing.
chronicle.current: He never asked his patron to shield him, and met the tribunals on his own standing.

log.rubric: THE TRIBUNAL · THE FIRST INQUISITION
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — three state inquisitions engineered by rival colleagues; he wins the first two
log.situation: The charge is framed around Qurʾan 2:102 and the angels at Babel who taught men magic: whatever you call your ʿilm al-ḥurūf, the prosecution says, this is what it descends from. Your accusers are colleagues. They have read you closely, which is the problem.

plate.caption: The fallen angels Hārūt and Mārūt, suspended at Babel — Iran, 16th–17th c. (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Distinguish theoretical lettrism from sorcery
options.detail: The core legal argument: a mathematics of letters is not an operation on spirits.

options.label: Answer with a creedal statement
options.detail: Give them orthodoxy in your own words — the apology as a genre.

options.label: Attack the accusers’ standing
options.detail: Name the jealousy. Aggressive, satisfying, and it escalates.

log.outcomeText: You write out a creed no jurist can fault, affirming everything required and abandoning nothing essential. The panel is satisfied and slightly disappointed.

chronicle.orig: He answered the first inquisition with a creed that satisfied the panel and conceded nothing that mattered.
chronicle.current: He answered the first inquisition with a creed that satisfied the panel and conceded nothing that mattered.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · A COURT STILL WRITES
log.source: RESEARCH — "applied lettrism remains an important technology of empire and personal advancement alike"; courts commissioned occult work from suspect scholars throughout
log.situation: A letter arrives under a careful seal: a provincial court — one that knows precisely what tribunals you have stood before — would like a protective inscription for a newborn prince. Discreetly. The same science being tried in one city is being commissioned from another, and nobody on either side finds this strange.

options.label: Compose the inscription
options.detail: Līmiyā, paid in silver and silence. Useful money; documentary evidence.

options.label: Send them the method, not the work
options.detail: Decline the commission; teach their own scholar to do it. Transmission over fee.

options.label: Burn the letter
options.detail: While tribunals sit, practice is evidence. Decline everything.

log.outcomeText: The letter burns well. So does the bridge — that court will not write twice.

chronicle.orig: He burned a court’s discreet commission unanswered, while the tribunals sat.
chronicle.current: He burned a court’s discreet commission unanswered, while the tribunals sat.

log.rubric: THE CIRCLE · THE LAST DOCUMENT
log.source: VN c39/c40 — the manner of his death is unrecorded; the testament is invented within the attested frame (dies 1432, impoverished, in legal limbo)
log.situation: Every scholar of your generation writes one: the testament — part will, part creed, part account rendered. Yours has a harder question inside it than most, because the thing you would bequeath is a condemned science and the people you would bequeath it to are safer without their names in your handwriting.

options.label: A public statement on the fate of the Investigations
options.detail: Defend the book one last time, in a document designed to be copied.

options.label: A quiet transmission to the Brethren alone
options.detail: No statement, no names, no evidence. The circle knows what it holds.

options.label: Leave no testament at all
options.detail: Let the work argue for itself or not at all. Silence as the last word.

log.outcomeText: Small packets, trusted hands, nothing signed. It is exactly as durable as the friendships are — which, it will turn out, is durable enough.

chronicle.orig: His testament went out in small unsigned packets, exactly as durable as his friendships.
chronicle.current: His testament went out in small unsigned packets, exactly as durable as his friendships.

log.rubric: THE PATRON’S DOOR · A QUIET ARRANGEMENT IS PROPOSED
log.source: Constructed; consistent with the documented pattern of pressure short of formal trial
log.situation: An intermediary suggests, over excellent tea, that all of this could end permanently. A short written statement withdrawing the more adventurous claims. No trial, no record, no exile. He is being kind. He is also entirely serious.

options.label: Sign the statement
options.detail: Peace, purchased with the part of the work that made it matter.

options.label: Refuse, politely
options.detail: Thank him and decline. He will report the refusal accurately.

options.label: Offer a narrower statement of your own drafting
options.detail: Concede vocabulary, keep the doctrine. The apologist’s craft.

log.outcomeText: He is not offended; he is a professional. The refusal is on the record by evening and everyone proceeds accordingly.

chronicle.orig: He declined the quiet arrangement, and the refusal was on record by evening.
chronicle.current: He declined the quiet arrangement, and the refusal was on record by evening.

log.rubric: THE ROAD · WHAT IS LEFT
log.source: BIOGRAPHY — five years of wandering exile after the third inquisition; death 1432, impoverished, in legal limbo
log.situation: However the tribunals fell out, the years after them are the ones that decide what this life was. There is a road, a diminishing amount of money, and a body of work that is either travelling without you or sitting in a box. What you do with the last of it is the last decision you get.

plate.caption: Teardrop cosmological diagram — Shams al-Maʿārif, p. 256 (Wikimedia Commons)

options.label: Teach wherever they let you stop
options.detail: Turn exile into transmission. No security, maximum spread.

options.label: Finish the work
options.detail: Complete the system, alone, whether or not anyone is left to read it.

options.label: Petition, negotiate, rebuild
options.detail: Spend the last years trying to get the standing back. It sometimes works.

options.label: Entrust everything to the circle and stop
options.detail: Hand it over. Let the movement be the movement; be an old man.

log.outcomeText: The last revisions are the best of them. Nobody sees the manuscript for four hundred years, and when they do it is complete.

chronicle.orig: He finished the system in exile, and it waited four centuries to be read entire.
chronicle.current: He finished the system in exile, and it waited four centuries to be read entire.
